sm: The episode opens with a preview of Culture Friday, a review of Disney's new film Hexed, and listener feedback. In the news, Ukraine could receive nearly 50 billion dollars from the European Union next year, but leaders must first agree on the loan. Swedish Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson said the EU cannot keep asking net contributors to pay more, and wants a smaller seven-year budget. Zelensky warned of another Russian attack on Ukraine's power grid, and crews are working to restore electricity in six regions. AAA expects nearly 82 million Americans to travel for Thanksgiving, a FedEx cargo jet ran off a runway at Miami International with no injuries, and in Egypt a speeding driver is detained after a crash near Cairo that killed at least 31 people. Culture Friday then begins with John Stonestreet discussing former Senator Ben Sasse's terminal pancreatic cancer.

Stonestreet describes Ben Sasse's call to live life backwards, meaning to face our mortality and so gain wisdom, which he says is neither despair nor hedonism. He ties this to Kierkegaard's line that life is lived forward but understood backwards, and to the big dot view of God's will, where God gives moral boundaries and expects us to make decisions. Turning to Grand Theft Auto 6, which brought nearly 4 billion dollars in first-day sales, the hosts say the crimes are imaginary but the game is practice in sinning. Stonestreet argues such games disproportionately affect young men, reflect a prolonged adolescence, and offer distraction rather than depth. He cites a teacher's idea that a good book takes you deeper into life while a bad one distracts you from it, and Josef Pieper's book on leisure.

The hosts mention a World Opinions piece by Ted Kluck calling the new Rocky film the spiritual opposite of Grand Theft Auto 6. Stonestreet hasn't seen it but says real, productive stories differ sharply from endless distraction, though not all entertainment should be dismissed. Next, a pastor wrote in about the story on forced child marriages among Muslims in Germany, asking how to think about subsidiarity and limits on the state, since similar reasoning could be used against Christian parents. Stonestreet points to Abraham Kuyper's idea of sphere sovereignty, in which the state, the home and the church each have their own authority. He says the state must step in when the family sphere breaks down, as with child marriage, abuse or neglect, and that this needs a sound moral framework, not neutrality.

The hosts introduce Disney's Hexed, the studio's first original story in three years after Strange World and Wish. Colin Garbarino reports that a teenager named Billy from Ohio is pulled through a portal into a land of witches and learns she can fly, with her secretive mother and a three-eyed cat named Beef helping her. The film is rated PG and has voice work from Hailee Steinfeld, Rashida Jones and Jodie Foster. He says it echoes the Disney Renaissance but has no songs, a breakneck pace, and no romance, and that it erases fathers and husbands entirely. He also objects that it explains away its villain's evil, praises the smooth animation, and calls the plot a tired, paint-by-numbers hero's journey. Listener feedback then begins with a pastor in Minnesota.

The pastor from Minnesota thanks World Radio for Arsenio Orteza's piece on Christian metal, saying bands like Skillet, Demon Hunter and Wolves at the Gate reach people who would never listen to standard Christian radio. Sherry from Myrtle Beach, a Taiwanese American, adds that dried seaweed is a daily staple in Taiwanese, Japanese and Korean diets with health benefits. Several listeners respond to Mary Reichard's two-part piece on vanity, including George, who quotes the C. S. Lewis passage about Susan in The Last Battle and praises the women in his life for aging gracefully. Richard McAdams says one key relationship where a spouse expresses appreciation is the antidote to insecurity, and he asks wives whether anti-aging treatments are for their husbands or for comparison with others. The hosts thank the production team, note this is episode 3540, and close with Psalm 119 verses 159 and 160.
